data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'saff' meaning pure or saffron, a spice derived from the crocus flower. The name Saffanah carries the meaning “Pure, Saffron” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Saffanah usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, saffron and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Saffanah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Saffron.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saffanah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Saffanah is believed to have originated from the old Arabic city of Saffar in Yemen, known for its production and trade of saffron. As a result, the name evolved to symbolize wealth, beauty, and exclusivity associated with the luxury spice.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic culture, saffron represents the purity, love, and spiritual enlightenment sought in the journey towards Allah. The name Saffanah also evokes the imagery of Rasool Allah (PBUH) and his companions' saffas (companionship groups) as a reminder of the collective duty of purifying and spreading knowledge and righteousness among society.
